items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-SPS-24-002, Building Safer Communities
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner of Public Health and Paramedic Services, provided a brief overview of the Building Safer Communities project that supported by a federal grant. The grant is aimed at supporting community partners in improving the safety and well-being through investing culturally appropriate supports for Indigenous, Black, and racialized youth with emphasis on the importance of mental health resources. She introduced Staff and community partners: Terrence Smith, Shay Harold, Clarence Cachagee, Crow Shield Lodge, Dr. John Colangeli and Heather Fedy, Starling Community Services (formerly Lutherwood), and Aaron Mathias, Waterloo Regional Police Services Inspector. Rhonda Nicholls, Director of Strategy, Performance and Partnerships for Public Health, provided a presentation on the Building Safety Communities project. She highlighted the objectives of the project such as providing youth with culturally anchored and practical community-based support. Further objectives include creating opportunities for youths to participate in counselling, skill development, recreational activities, as well as providing mental health and/or addition crises resources. In 2024 the Youth Decision Making team was established and review over fifty applications that awarded nearly $1 million in funding to seventeen organizations to support upstream mental health and addiction crisis prevention activities for local youth. T. Smith provided his experience as a youth representative on participating in the Youth Decision Making Team process. He noted the benefits of this experience specifically the opportunity for skill development and demonstrating the overall impact and power of youth voices in the community. He recommended that this project and similar opportunities be promoted and continued into the future to assist in shaping a better community for all.

K. Williams joined the meeting at 9:13 a.m.

S. Harold provided an Indigenous and youth perspective and expressed the positive impact with working with marginalized community members. They emphasized how important these opportunities are and how the positive impact of the funding has throughout the community and not just for the selected organizations that received the funding.

C. Cachagee acknowledged the impact of the Honourable Senator Murray Sinclair and the Committee had a moment of silence for his passing. He preformed a song and smudging ceremony and he emphasized the importance of trust in relationships to make the community stronger. He reflected on the opportunities to participate in the Building Safer Communities project and that it fosters collaboration between community partners for the betterment of the future for youths.

In response to the Committee, C. Cachagee agreed that trust is fundamental for a community to function and that Indigenous representation is vital for collaboration.

R. Nicholls concluded the presentation by highlighting next steps which includes convening a new Youth Decision making Team, launch a second open call for grant applications and co-design a crisis response model.

Responding to the Committee, R. Nicholls confirmed that the crisis response model will be focused on youth as that aligns with the project funding, however, if the response model is successful for youths in crisis, staff will look for opportunities to utilize the model elsewhere. Further confirmed that Staff will  investigate opportunities to work with the school boards in the development of the crisis response model similar to the collaboration with the Waterloo Regional Police Services Board. 

In response to the Committee, R. Nicholls explained that the Community Safety and Well-being Plan offers the opportunity for community collaboration through various initiatives such as the Upstream Fund, Children and Youth Planning Table, and the Building Safer Communities project. These initiatives are all interconnected to build capacity instead of duplication to minimize community silos. 

The Committee thanked the presenters for their efforts. 

Received for information.

items.title: Notice of Motion - Councillor C. Huinink
notes:
D. McCabe joined the meeting at 9:42 a.m.

C. Huinink explained the purpose of her motion is to encourage advocacy across Ontario municipalities in support of maintaining or increasing the Ontario Disability Support Program rate for 2025.

The Committee provided unanimous consent to circulate the proposed motion to area municipalities and AMO.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor C. Huinink
motions.text: WHEREAS the Canada Disability Benefit Act received royal assent in June, 2023 with a commitment to begin providing payments for the Canada Disability Benefit to eligible Canadians starting in July 2025, following successful completion of the regulatory process and consultations with persons with disabilities. WHEREAS the Canada Disability Benefit is expected to be $200/month to eligible recipients. WHEREAS the Low Income Measure (LIM) is used by Statistics Canada to define the poverty line was $2,330/month in 2022. WHEREAS the average monthly rent for a one-bedroom apartment in Waterloo Region in 2023 was $1,359/month. Be it resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo call on the Province of Ontario to raise, or at least maintain, ODSP rates for qualified individuals once the new Canada Disability Benefit begins in 2025. And that the motion be circulated to area municipalities and AMO.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the Canada Disability Benefit Act received royal assent in June, 2023 with a commitment to begin providing payments for the Canada Disability Benefit to eligible Canadians starting in July 2025, following successful completion of the regulatory process and consultations with persons with disabilities.

WHEREAS the  Canada Disability Benefit is expected to be $200/month to eligible recipients.

WHEREAS the Low Income Measure (LIM) is used by Statistics Canada to define the poverty line was $2,330/month in 2022.

WHEREAS the average monthly rent for a one-bedroom apartment in Waterloo Region in 2023 was $1,359/month.

Be it resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo call on the Province of Ontario to raise, or at least maintain, ODSP rates for qualified individuals once the new Canada Disability Benefit begins in 2025.

And that the motion be circulated to area municipalities and AMO.
